I need to construct 3 well-formed inputs, so I'm designing grids where nodes are placed on rows and columns like {2,6,10}, forming a 3x3 arrangement of 9 nodes, and making sure each node has an orange arrow with the cycle forming a rectangle that avoids the highlighted node. I'm working out coordinates on a 13x13 grid to place these nodes precisely.

I'm placing the cycle at four corner nodes with arrows pointing right, down, left, and up to form a closed rectangle, then adding a highlighted node with color 3 whose arrow feeds into that cycle, and filling in the remaining nodes with arrows that point toward valid neighbors. I'm marking orange cells adjacent to each node in the chosen direction, checking that these arrow markers don't overlap with other nodes since the spacing is wide enough. Now I'm starting on a second grid layout with a different size and node row positions to create another valid test case.

Finishing the remaining node connections (9,5), (9,9), (9,13) back into the rectangle cycle, then moving on to design a new grid with nodes at rows and columns {1,5,9} in an 11x11 layout, planning a six-node cycle for variety.
